flags.name: Gravy Mix Rich Brown
flags.issue: Name is truncated and the pack size went with it. The invoice line reads 'GRAVY MIX RICH BROWN G/FREE' + '7KG Executive Chef' across two rows; only the first row was captured, so the product entered the feed as 'Gravy Mix Rich Brown' with pack_qty null, needs_pack_review true, and a cost of $57.6087 per 'ea'. Foodlink's UOM column only ever says EA/CTN, so the description is the ONLY place the pack size is stated — losing it loses the rate.
flags.suggested_fix: Pack is 7 kg -> $8.23/kg. NOT GUESSED: confirmed from two independent sources already in our own data. (1) Foodlink invoice SI4483241, 2026-07-24, same code 101239, where the words did not wrap: 'GRAVY MIX RICH BROWN G/FREE 7KG Executive Chef', stored as 7 kg at $8.2300/kg. (2) The Lightspeed recipe seed, ProductID 22888768, 'Gravy Mix Rich Brown G/Free 7kg Executive Chef' at $7.8611/kg. The root cause is fixed in the parser today (see parser_regression.py triage item 33) and this row should re-read correctly on the next Foodlink delivery; no manual edit made, and none needed if that holds.
flags.money: a recipe costing gravy off the sizeless row books ~7x

flags.name: Broccolini / Broccolini (BROCE)
flags.issue: Two picker entries for the same vegetable from the same supplier. BRL is a box costed at 12 ea for $33.60 = $2.80 each (pack_parsed_as 'chef-confirmed'); BROCE is a single bunch at $3.17, disambiguated with its own code by the 2026-08-15 collapse rule because the pack units differ ('ea' vs 'bunch') and the rates are 13% apart, just outside the 10% merge window. The chef now sees broccolini twice.
flags.suggested_fix: NOT GUESSED — needs Zak or the chef to confirm the one fact that decides it: is an FFT 'bunch' (BROCE) the same physical unit as one of the 12 in a BRL box? The two rates agreeing to within 13% suggests yes, and if so BROCE's pack unit should be 'ea' so the two collapse. If a market bunch is genuinely bigger, both rows are correct and should stay — that is exactly the case the 10%/pack-unit guard exists to protect (triage item 13, where merging deleted two market bunches).
flags.money: none directly; a duplicate picker entry, and a 13% cost swing depending which the chef picks
